blocks.x: A working definition of K-12 & School Systems for Education & Research: engineered controls, named owners, weekly evidence, and a signed baseline so every claim of improvement can be replayed line by line.
Before proposing anything, we map the context K-12 & School Systems will run in — regulators, decision cadence, existing contracts — because the design that ignores context fails at the gate.

blocks.note: The pipeline is measured end to end; each stage reports its own freshness and cost, which is what makes the unit economics arguable.

blocks.x: We engineer K-12 & School Systems so that regressions are cohorts, not surprises: each stage owns its latency budget and failure policy, and rollback is rehearsed before go-live rather than after the incident.

blocks.x: Failure modes & the guards we ship

items: Metric anarchy
One definition per metric, owned and versioned — the dashboard and the board pack cannot disagree.
Silent schema drift
Contracts enforced at the boundary — schema drift fails the pipeline loudly, in minutes.
Cost creep
Unit costs on a published budget with alerts at the threshold — creep is caught by the meter, not by the invoice.
